_note: Hosts and calling the banners (war-and-realm §2.1-2.5; game-design §12.3-12.4). PLACEHOLDER numbers.

levy._note: Levies are drawn from young men only: each own settlement gives per_thousand levy units per 1,000 people (times turnout), at most max_per_settlement, of its culture's levy unit (data/rosters.json levy; the generic peasant_levy otherwise). While they serve, the settlement's income drops by production_drop per unit (at most max_drop) and returns when they are disbanded. Total population is kept (war-and-realm §2.1).

standing._note: Turnout and muster speed by the ruler's standing (war-and-realm §2.2): turns until the levies set out, turnout share, field loyalty (low: each levy unit may desert, desertion per turn, and contingents refuse dangerous orders). No extra resource.

detachment._note: Captain-led detachments (game-design §12.3): at most max_units units, defend only, foreign_factor of the movement allowance outside friendly land, and they merge into a lord's army of their faction on contact (within merge_radius metres).

foreign_factor._note: Movement allowance outside friendly land (war-and-realm §2.6: fast in own and allied land, slow in enemy land; military access counts as allied).

zoc._note: Large armies block passage (war-and-realm §2.6): a field army blocks cells within block_radius (data/movement.json) plus per_unit metres per unit beyond from_units, at most max_radius.

vassal_turnout._note: A vassal sends its strongest field army to the muster point with chance its reliability x the liege's turnout (war-and-realm §2.2: each vassal's turnout also scales with its own loyalty).

_notice_note: Mustering is visible to the world: factions with a settlement within notice_metres of the muster point learn of it (chronicle and AI wariness).
